title: Pi vs Claude Code trial: scorecard and pass mark
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-11: judge whether Pi is fit to use vs Claude Code, on real Loka work.

Setup: same model both sides (Opus 5.5); alternate comparable M9/M9b/M10 rows between harnesses; reviewer briefs and commits do not name the harness. ~2 weeks.

Per finished task, one comment: harness | task id | first review verdict | fix rounds | CI green first push (y/n) | rule breaks (redaction, --no-verify, self-computed expected values, skipped self-review, spec not updated) | owner interventions | cost (Pi: API $; CC: weekly bar delta) | start->merge time.

Pass mark (set up front): Pi is fit if rule breaks and fix rounds are no worse than Claude Code, owner interventions no higher, and cost per task is within the owner's limit (owner to set).

Known Pi gaps at start: Claude SessionStart hook (Beads status) does not run; .claude/agents definitions and per-agent model routing are not used (reviewer.md pasted into prompts; children inherit the parent model); no /code-review skill (AGENTS.md self-review); an extension refused the API key until PI_BG_FEATURES dropped attribution.

title: Research: offload heavy checks and the mechanics track from the M1 to cloud compute
description: Owner 2026-10-09 (verbatim excerpt): 'i wonder if we should rent a beefy server for a month so we can get faster CI ... look around for something that would significantly speed up our stuff and offload the processor intensive tasks from the macbook air m1 so the m1 can focus on ui polish things and mechanics stuff can have speedy cloud server'. Research brief: compare (a) faster hosted CI runners (GitHub larger runners, Blacksmith, Depot, Namespace, Ubicloud, BuildJet, and whatever 'useJog' refers to), (b) a rented dedicated/cloud box (Hetzner, OVH, AWS/GCP spot, etc.) used as a self-hosted runner and/or a remote dev box where mechanics-track agents run Claude Code + worktrees + bin/check_all.sh, (c) Claude Code cloud/remote sessions. Inputs: bin/check_all.sh, .githooks/pre-push, .github/workflows/*.yml, mise toolchain (Elixir/Erlang, Node, Playwright Chromium). Output: ranked recommendation with monthly cost, expected speed-up, setup effort, security (secrets, GitHub token scope), and what changes in our workflow. Read-only; no purchases, no sign-ups.
notes:
Result 2026-10-09: first pick rent a Linux box for the mechanics agents (Hetzner CCX43 hourly trial, then AX102 ~EUR257/mo); Jog (usejog.com) = cheap GitHub runners, <$5/mo, small vendor; Claude Code cloud sessions not ready (4 vCPU, no Erlang/Elixir, Node 22 only, gh pr blocked by proxy). Owner questions open: region, gate, Jog vendor trust, rental length.
Owner 2026-10-09: budget max $20/month; no Jog, use GitHub free hosted CI.

title: Engine: death outside a combat round (bleed tick, drain) narrates nothing
description: Showcase combat playtest (loka-y6yg.7) G2/G3. A death that is not a combat round narrates nothing. Only combat writes a death line (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_flow.ts:232, world.combat.narration.player_died); the death sequence itself (mechanics/death/sequence.ts) adds no narration. So a bleed tick at hp 1 (G3: the player pressed Take a purse, the tick ran first, as designed) or any drain kill moves the body to the shrine in silence; the next screen is the inn at full hp. Not loka-x2gv (that is a conflicting_write fault). Smallest fix: an optional authored world.death narration key (e.g. "You fall, and wake at the inn.") that the death sequence appends once for the player's body for every cause, with combat keeping its own line (do not double it); Book routes it to World.

BRIEF (drafted 2026-10-08, PM-approved for assignment; developer Opus, designer consult for book-ui.md sentence, Opus review + second opinion because existing saves change behavior):
# Brief: loka-8mm — world time starts when the player first enters the world

Base: `main` 9acaf2b5. Beads: `loka-8mm`. Lane: **Hosted PR** (must merge alone; `bin/check_all.sh`
once, pre-push hook is the final run, ready PR, fresh reviewer once CI is green, merge per
WORKFLOW step 7). Developer: Opus. Lessons: `docs/lessons/mechanics.md` (check every committed
intermediate state with the real save loader), `docs/lessons/mobile.md`.

## Goal

The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): world time starts as soon as the player enters the
world for the first time. No time passes while the ancestry screen is shown. This reverses the
2026-10-06 ruling
(`docs/decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md`, "Allow elapsed updates").
Source: the question at `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-e2-gate-fable-audit.md:58-61`. Today
`stepElapsed` (`kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:167-180`) skips the ancestry gate that `step`
applies (`:126-131`). As a result, 2 minutes on the ancestry screen is 6000 units at rate 50.

## Decision: what "first entry into the world" is

First entry is the **accepted `choose_ancestry` decision**, which writes the `character.select`
row. The predicate is the existing `needsAncestry(world, actor)` at
`kernel/ts/src/commands/actions.ts:55-56`:
`!!world.cartridge.ancestries && !characterChoice(world, actor)`. It is the same condition that
`step` inlines at `world.ts:126-131` and that `refusal()` uses at `actions.ts:192-193`. On a
cartridge with no `ancestries`, first entry is world creation and the gate does nothing. The
ferry, scene, sampler and pre-v038 missing_child fixtures are therefore unchanged.

Room entry is not a separate event. The player is placed in the entry room at creation
(`mechanics.md:40-44`), and the ancestry choice is the first thing the player can do there.

## Required changes (smallest complete set)

1. **Kernel gate.** Export `needsAncestry` from `actions.ts`. In `step`, replace the inline
   condition with it (no behavior change). In `stepElapsed`, add
   `if (needsAncestry(world, world.character)) return reject('invalid_state');`. Put it after
   the validate, `identity` and command-id checks, so malformed or foreign elapsed commands keep
   their current codes, and before the owner/capability lookup. Every replay path inherits the
   gate with no extra code: `mobile/authority/local-story/delivery.ts:63`,
   `receipt-history.ts:35`, `kernel/ts/play/run.ts:74` and `kernel/ts/test/e1_case_host.ts:24`.
2. **Driver: no credit before the choice.** The kernel gate alone is not enough. The app ticks
   every 250 ms whenever it is active (`mobile/app/App.tsx:99-112`), and nothing checks
   ancestry (`elapsed.ts`, `delivery.ts`, `App.tsx`, `session.ts`, `invocation.ts`,
   `authority.ts`). With only the kernel gate:
   - every pulse on the ancestry screen would be rejected;
   - `ClockDriver.advance` would turn that rejection into a fault (`elapsed.ts:130-131`), and
     the Book would show "Time stopped: invalid_state" (`presenter.ts:48`, `Book.tsx:192`);
   - after the choice, the wall time spent on the ancestry screen would still be credited,
     because `capture` uses `mono - baseline` or `wall - old.wall_ms` (`elapsed.ts:107-111`).

   **Fix:** in `ClockDriver.capture` (`elapsed.ts:90-115`), set `d = 0` (the computation at `:107-111`) while
   `needsAncestry(this.s.world, this.s.world.character)` holds. `accounted(old, 0, rate, wall)`
   then re-anchors the wall clock and the monotonic baseline with no credit
   (`elapsed-store.ts:68-79`). The target stays at the head, so `drain` never delivers elapsed
   before the choice.

   The `choose_ancestry` invocation already reserves time through
   `driver.reserve` → `capture('active')` (`invocation.ts:91-95`). That capture happens before
   the choice commits, so it anchors the baseline at the moment of choice. Time credited after
   that starts exactly at the choice. No new state, timer or row is needed.
3. **Decision record.** Add `docs/decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md`.
   It records the owner answer marked (paraphrased), the predicate above, and the save impact
   below. Add one line to the 2026-10-06 record:
   `Superseded 2026-10-08 by [world time starts at entry](owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md).`
4. **Optional, only if it is one line:** the `payload.type !== 'elapsed'` exemption at
   `actions.ts:192` becomes unreachable, because `step` refuses elapsed at `world.ts:125`. Leave
   it unless deleting it is a one-token change that tests still cover.

## Spec amendment (spec first, same PR)

- **`docs/system/mechanics.md:303`.** Replace the paragraph with:
  > Under the [owner's world-time ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md), world time starts when the player first enters the world: the accepted selection. Before selection, `stepElapsed` refuses trusted elapsed updates as `invalid_state`, as Step refuses ordinary commands, so the clock and due jobs stay at the birth clock. The local driver credits no wall time before selection; credited time starts at the selection invocation's reservation. This supersedes the [2026-10-06 pre-choice elapsed ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md).
- **`mechanics.md:43-44`.** Change "precedes ordinary player commands, while trusted elapsed
  updates retain their separately authorized admission." to "precedes ordinary player commands
  and trusted elapsed updates; world time starts at selection."
- **`docs/system/save.md:229` (M1-A).** After "A new command passes `stepElapsed`", add
  "(which refuses `invalid_state` before [D11 selection](mechanics.md#d11-character-choice-selected-contract), matching Step)".
- **`save.md` "Durable elapsed sessions" (after `:236`).** Add: "Before D11 selection a capture
  re-anchors wall and monotonic evidence with zero credit; the target stays at the confirmed
  head, so no elapsed command is delivered."
- **`docs/system/protocol.md:69-70` (Step order item 5).** Append: "`stepElapsed` applies the
  same gate to trusted elapsed (`invalid_state`)."
- **`docs/system/book-ui.md:458` (D11 interaction).** Add: "World time does not run while the
  picker is shown; it starts at the accepted choice." The clauses at `:454`, `:744` and `:923`
  ("the world clock continues while the page is open", and similar) describe play after
  selection and stay as they are. **The designer writes this sentence**, because the designer is
  the single writer of Book UI spec text.
- **`mechanics.md:584` (M1-A).** Add "before D11 selection" to the `stepElapsed` `invalid_state`
  refusals.
- **`docs/system/owner-rules.md:44`** ("Backgrounding does not pause the world"). Append a
  linked note: "World time starts at first entry (D11 selection); before it there is no world
  clock to pause ([2026-10-08](../decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md))."
  This is a pointer, not a new rule.
- GameView (`protocol.md:366`, `time`) does not change shape.

## Composition record (architecture.md "Building mechanics by composition")

- **Real consumer:** `ClockDriver` (`mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts`). The Book status
  time shows only after selection (`Book.tsx:177-190`, hidden while `view.ancestry_choices`);
  the "Catching up…" line at `Book.tsx:191` is not hidden.
- **Shared reads:** the `characters` row through `needsAncestry` / `characterChoice`
  (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:13`, exported as `choice`).
- **Typed writes:** none new. The elapsed checkpoint row keeps its shape; before selection only
  `wall_ms` is re-anchored.
- **Writer ownership:** unchanged. The schedule rule owns elapsed, and attributes owns
  `character.select`.
- **Reused primitives:** `needsAncestry`, the `invalid_state` refusal, `accounted(...)` with
  `d = 0`, and the existing reserve-on-invoke.
- **Missing invariant:** "no clock credit before selection". The kernel enforces it at the
  trust boundary, and the driver enforces it at the source.
- **Composes without code:** receipt replay (`receipt-history.ts`), `kernel/ts/play/run.ts`,
  the E1 host and ActionSet admission.
- **Named-mechanic / content exceptions:** none.
- **Review lens:**
  - *Ordering:* reserve-capture precedes the choice commit.
  - *Atomic rollback:* unchanged.
  - *Trust boundary:* kernel gate placed after identity.
  - *Shared admission:* one predicate for step, refusal, ActionSet and stepElapsed.
  - *Changed-row save/reopen:* no new rows (see save impact).

## Save impact (pre-production rules: `owner-decision-forward-development-2026-10-05.md:7-16`)

The release pin is the cartridge `content_hash` (`authority.ts:92-99`), so this kernel change
does not change any pin. Existing chapter-one saves from older builds fall into three cases:

- **(a) Nearly every existing device save of chapter one has accepted pre-choice elapsed
  receipts.** The old driver delivered elapsed on every 250 ms active pulse while the ancestry
  screen was shown.
  - *Plain reopen:* opens cleanly. The clock it already committed stays as saved, with no
    rewrite. The driver credits nothing more until the choice.
  - *Reopen through `receiptHistory`* (`exchange-save.ts:25`, `liquid-save.ts:30`, used once
    exchange or liquid history exists): **every such save refuses**, and the label it shows
    says malformed or corrupt. The forward-development policy permits this, so it does not
    block. State it plainly in the PR body so the owner is not surprised to see "corrupt" on
    their own device save. The replay now rejects those receipts, so it throws
    `SyntaxError('malformed JSON: inconsistent accepted history')` (`receipt-history.ts:18-20`).
    This is an **explicit refusal**, never a silent change. The developer must confirm the
    host code it surfaces as (expected `save_corrupt`), state it in the PR, and add **no**
    compatibility code.
- **(b) Older save that closed with pending pre-choice debt** (checkpoint `target > clock`
  before selection). After the change, capture credits 0 but keeps the old target. `drain`
  then delivers, the kernel rejects it, and the Book shows "Time stopped: invalid_state".
  `reserve` drains the existing debt before any invocation, so `choose_ancestry` itself fails
  too. The only way out is Start over, which `Fault` offers for every fault
  (`Book.tsx:192`, `:229-238`). That is explicit, not silent. Record it in the PR.
  Do not clamp the target. Clamping would change a save, and it would add machinery that
  exists only for old data.
- **(c) New saves:** no pre-choice receipts or debt exist.

Under the user's rule, a second-opinion review is needed only if save or reconcile behavior
changes. Reopen of old saves does change, by refusing case (a), so **add the second opinion**.

## Tests and fixtures

**Must change**

- `kernel/ts/test/character_choice.test.ts:71-109`, "trusted elapsed drains a due job before
  ancestry choice…". It pins the reversed rule. Rewrite it as the kernel test in Acceptance 1,
  keeping its independent values (until `68400`, job `fen_hounds` due at `68400`).

**Checked, expected unchanged (they choose before elapsed)**

- `kernel/ts/test/sim_mechanics.test.ts:105`
- `r9c_creatures_transport.test.ts:57`
- `kernel/ts/test/r9c_elapsed_jobs.test.ts:141`
- `mobile/authority/local-story/r9c_elapsed_jobs.test.ts:158`
- `mobile/authority/local-story/r9c_faults.test.ts:81`
- `e1_creatures.ts:46`
- `deer_fixture.ts:35`
- the E1 cases (spot-checked)
- `mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.test.ts` (ferry/scene, no ancestries)
- the transcripts `cartridges/ashmere_missing_child/transcripts/{light,population}.jsonl`
  (pins v021 and d8_trace, both before ancestries)

**Owner answer (d)** (`owner-decision-e2-plan-2026-10-07.md:14`): any r9c synthetic answer that
breaks is updated in this slice, with the reason in the PR. No r9c test is expected to break.

**Unverified:** `e1_rejoin.ts:37` elapsed. It depends on whether `search()` reaches
`e1_paths.ts:14` choose first. If it does not, that case fails, and the developer reports it by
name.

## Acceptance (literal values)

1. **Kernel test**, in `character_choice.test.ts`, replacing `:71-109`. *Breaks: elapsed
   bypasses the D11 gate again.*
   - Setup: fresh v035+ancestries world `w`, run `6f6f6f6f-1111-4222-8333-444444444444`,
     `until = 68400`.
   - Before the choice, `stepElapsed(w, elapsed(from w.state.clock, until 68400), 1)`:
     - `decision` deep-equals `{ kind: 'rejected', error: { code: 'invalid_state' } }`;
     - `result.world === w`.
   - Then `choose_ancestry fen_born` at revision 1 is accepted.
   - The same span at revision 2 is then accepted:
     - `clock === 68400`;
     - the `fen_hounds` job due at `68400` has status `'completed'`.
   - A malformed or foreign elapsed command before selection still returns its old code. Keep
     one assertion: wrong `world_context_id` → `not_found`.
2. **Driver test**, in `mobile/authority/local-story`. *Breaks: ancestry-screen wall time is
   credited later, or the driver faults on the ancestry screen.*
   - Setup: r9c_interactions cartridge (rate `50`, start `64800`, ancestries), fake clocks.
   - At wall/mono `0`, pulse `'resume'`.
   - Advance `120000` ms, then pulse `'active'`:
     - `world().state.clock === 64800`;
     - status `{ kind: 'ready' }`;
     - no elapsed receipt row.
   - Invoke `choose_ancestry fey_touched`; it is accepted.
   - Advance `60000` ms, then pulse `'active'` until status is ready (at most 16 commits per
     drain): `clock === 64800 + 3000 = 67800`. The old behavior gives `73800`.
   - If a due r9c job boundary splits the span, assert the same final `67800`.
   - Add one resume line: close at `120000` before the choice, reopen with the wall clock at
     `3600000`, pulse `'resume'` → `clock === 64800`.
3. **Red controls**, run and quoted in the PR:
   - (i) delete the kernel gate line → Acceptance 1 fails on `accepted !== rejected`;
   - (ii) delete the driver `d = 0` branch → Acceptance 2 fails, at `70800` or "Time stopped:
     invalid_state".
4. **E1 recorder stays at 38 of 38.** Run
   `node kernel/ts/test/e1_cases.ts tmp/e1-selected-v042.json <dir>` (selection per
   `docs/evidence/2026-10-07-e1-coverage-complete/README.md:11-12`). Expected:
   `pass: 38 real SQLite cases passed`. Otherwise report exactly which case or path failed or
   reopened differently.
5. **Narrow runs:** the tests above, plus `kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts`, kernel and mobile
   `r9c_elapsed_jobs`, `r9c_faults`, `sim_mechanics` and `elapsed.test.ts`. Then
   `bin/check_all.sh` once.
6. **PR body** includes: the save-impact cases (a)–(c), with the host code that case (a)
   surfaces as; the plain warning that existing device saves with exchange or liquid history
   will refuse; the superseded decision; "no pin removed".

## Designer

**Consult.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md:231` says a slice that changes what the player sees consults the
designer for its brief, its Book UI spec text and its review. This slice changes what the player
sees in two small ways:

- "Catching up…" (`Book.tsx:191`) no longer appears on the ancestry screen.
- The first time shown after the choice is the chapter start time, not start plus dwell time.

No new element, wording or layout is added. The designer's scope is small:

- write the `book-ui.md:458` sentence;
- confirm that no design-system change is needed;
- review the UI-visible behavior in the PR.

## Scope trigger (stop and ask)

- Any change to the save format, the checkpoint row shape, a protocol or GameView shape, or the
  ErrorCode set.
- `kernel_api` in `INSTALLED`: do not bump it. No documented bump rule exists, and recent bumps
  came with new capabilities (`git log -S"kernel_api: '1.3"`). If a check demands a bump, stop
  and ask.
- Any need for a migration, a clamp or compatibility code for old saves.
- Any E1 case that falls below 38/38 and cannot be explained by this rule.

## Process rules (copy)

- Self-review is ONE pass: `/code-review medium`.
- Narrow mutant runs only (the two red controls). Full-suite mutation sweeps happen only before
  a release (owner rule).
- Run long commands in the background, without polling.
- Review: one fresh Opus reviewer, plus a second opinion (save reopen behavior changes for old
  saves).
- Ponytail before implementation and Ponytail Review before handoff.

## Out of scope

- New UI elements, a clock on the ancestry screen, migrating old saves, and the `actions.ts:192`
  cleanup beyond one token.

Question first: does save.md require reopen to refuse a head clock earlier than the latest committed receipt? If yes: one forge+reopen test (narrow run, red control); if the check is missing in code, that is a production fix slice.
notes:
Owner 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): answer at the pre-polish Fable audit triage.
Audit B facts (2026-10-08): (1) no docs/system clause requires refusing a head clock earlier than the newest receipt; receipts carry no clock (store.ts:36-46,55-58; nearest save.md:129-131,:472,:956-958). (2) Enforced indirectly by replay: receipt-history.ts:41 same(world.state, saved.state) and :31 revision pin, gated per loka-b60; deadline-save.ts:155-160. (3) Forge on chapter v042 (rev 2 clock 64800): clock-1, clock+1, revision-1, newest receipt deleted -> all save_corrupt, bytes untouched. Auditor suggests close as enforced by replay + fix loka-b60.
Owner 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): yes, reopen must refuse a head clock behind the newest receipt. Already enforced by replay; work = one save.md sentence + loka-b60 (unconditional receiptHistory) + one forge+reopen test expecting save_corrupt (red control). Close with the pre-polish PR.

  `per_100` (refused * 100 / commands, two decimals as a string, like flows' band), and refused
  counts by error code, by room definition key (where the player stood), and by command (payload
  type, plus `:<action key>` for a cartridge action).
- Drift: for each refused candidate, run the view invariant `gameview_agrees_with_admission`
  (kernel/ts/src/view/invariants_view.ts:31) on {view: gameView(before), command, decision,
  resolves, action_key}, resolves built as test/sim.ts:269-271. Accepted candidates are already
  checked by flows' `checked` (it throws). Report `drift: {count, first: [up to 5 {seed, step,
  room, command, code}]}`.
- X3 from accepted steps: `revisits` per room key (entries minus one; the start room's first
  entry counts as an entry), `moves` and `backtracks` (an accepted step that changes the room back
  to the room the player left on the previous room change), `new_facts: {count,
  median_steps_between}` where a new fact is an accepted step after which world.state.facts holds
  a key it did not hold or a different value, and steps are counted from the run start or the
  previous new fact (median null when none). Integers, no rates beyond per_100.
- A report, not a check: no CI gate (gating is loka-kgd.107.3, owner question open).

COMPOSITION RECORD
Consumer: authors; .107.3 gates later (may gate drift.count = 0). Reads: flows' run, each
candidate's DecisionResult (rejected.error.code), GameView, resolved actions, world rooms and
facts. Writes: nothing (stdout). Reused: flows run/worker/first/delivered, sim `checked`,
`gameview_agrees_with_admission`, canonical encode. New: play/friction.ts and one hook.

FILES (read only these ranges)
- kernel/ts/play/flows.ts (271 lines): opts :79-80, run() :114-147, first() :155-165, labelOf
  :202, CLI :254-271 (copy its flag handling shape). Add `observe` only.
- New kernel/ts/play/friction.ts (<= 300 lines; functions <= 40).
- kernel/ts/test/sim.ts:213-236 (`checked`), :260-275 (the obs and resolves);
  kernel/ts/src/view/invariants_view.ts:31; kernel/ts/test/sim.test.ts:399-418 (planted views
  that trip the invariant: the pattern for the drift test).
- New kernel/ts/test/friction.test.ts: compile cartridges/standing_sampler with `mix
  loka.compile` into a mkdtemp and load it (kernel/ts/test/flows.test.ts:19-28).
- docs/toolbox.gen.json / docs/system-graph.gen.json only if contracts --check asks.

ACCEPTANCE (hand-derived from cartridges/standing_sampler: entry square; square exits only east
to gate, gate exits only west to square; a Move with no exit is not_found (mechanics.md:67); mv
start 100, a move costs 1 mv and no time; calendar start 25200, 3600 per hour; the apple lies in
square and item_acquired{item apple} adjusts the fact trust (reactions/gift_apple.json); seeds 1,
days 1)
a. Pace policy: candidates [move north, move east, move west, wait clock+3600] while the clock is
   below C0 + 4 hours, then [] (the run ends). Per hour: square north refused, east accepted;
   gate north refused, (east skipped this hour), west accepted; square north refused, (east, west
   skipped), wait accepted. Four hours: commands 24, refused 12, per_100 "50.00", by code
   {not_found: 12}, by room {square: 8, gate: 4}, by command {move: 12}, drift count 0.
b. Same run, X3: moves 8, backtracks 7 (every move but the first returns to the room left),
   revisits {square: 4, gate: 3}, new_facts count 0, median null.
c. Fetch policy: step 1 [move east], step 2 [move west], step 3 [take the apple], then []:
   commands 3, refused 0, new_facts count 1, median_steps_between 3.
d. Drift: a planted view (sim.test.ts:399-418 style) listing the gate exit as available while
   the step refuses invalid_state (or a refused decision fed to the exported drift function on a
   planted view, whichever needs no test-only production parameter): drift count 1, its first
   entry names room square, command move, code invalid_state. Hand-count it; never read the
   expected value from friction's output.
e. flows unchanged: kernel/ts/test/flows.test.ts passes untouched (the hook is optional).
f. CLI on the compiled sampler with --seeds 1 --days 1 exits 0 and prints JSON that decodes with
   a `refused` field; a bad flag exits 2.

RED CONTROLS (each must fail a named test)
- observe called only for accepted candidates -> a (refused 0).
- by-room counts accepted commands too -> a (by room {square: 16, gate: 8}).
- per_100 over accepted instead of all commands -> a ("100.00").
- drift run on accepted instead of refused candidates -> d.
- backtrack compared to the current room instead of the one left -> b.
- new fact counted on every step that writes any fact, or steps not reset -> c.

FOCUSED RUNS
`node --test kernel/ts/test/friction.test.ts kernel/ts/test/flows.test.ts`. Not the full suite.
play/ tools are fast: plain step for candidates, `checked` only on accepted steps; keep it so

title: Toolbox row 17: ranged combat (batch M9b)
notes:
Written 2026-10-12 04:35 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (brief drafter)

BRIEF loka-kgd.110: toolbox row 17, ranged combat (batch M9b). Size M, one developer run, no split (engine plus sampler; no new Book element).

GOAL
Owner answer 2 (docs/decisions/owner-decision-mechanics-toolbox-2026-10-08.md:37; docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:54): ranged combat starts with a same-room first strike. Shooting into adjacent rooms comes later and is out of scope. Row text (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:150): "bow strikes first at a foe in the same room; ammo consumed; melee follows". Deps 6a and G2 are done (#366, #351).

LANE
Batch M9b item lane, as M9 ran it. Branch toolbox/m9b-ranged off toolbox/batch-m9b (head d461c38e), in your own worktree under worktrees.noindex; run bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Commit and do not push. Hand the branch and exact head to the PM, who runs a PR-less Opus item review and merges the item into the batch. Hosted CI runs on the batch PR head. Locally, run only the focused tests listed below, under nice -n 10.

SPEC GAP: FIRST TASK IS THE docs/system AMENDMENT (same branch, its own first commit)
docs/system has no ranged mechanic. combat@1 says Attack "does not attack immediately, advance time or draw RNG" (docs/system/mechanics.md:736-740) and "Odd rounds give the player the first opportunity" (mechanics.md:751-752). Cite the row text and the owner answer above.

Add a section "## Ranged first strike (toolbox row 17)" at the end of docs/system/mechanics.md, after "Movement on a status (toolbox row SR7)", in the bullet shape of 6a and 6b (mechanics.md:2110-2121, 2253-2267). Also add a one-sentence pointer at mechanics.md:751. Decided design:
- Shot. A shot happens in an encounter's round 1 (the encounter row's `round` is 1; foundation/compose_encounter.ts:44) when all of these hold at the player's turn:
  - the player wields an item whose `weapon` has `ranged {ammo}`;
  - the weapon's skill is usable (as G2, mechanics.md:1872-1873);
  - the player's body holds at least 1 in the ammo resource pool;
  - the existing turn guards pass: standing, and statusAllows 'attack' (SR4).
  The player's opportunity is then the shot. It uses the weapon's own `attack` profile, with G2 kind, crit and the item's tags as materials, plus row 2 bonuses. Attack admission and Attack itself are unchanged: still no RNG at Attack.
- Foe waits. The foe's round-1 opportunity is skipped exactly when the shot was taken, hit or miss. This covers the ordinary round's NPC and the pack round's selected member. The pack cursor, round order and successor job are unchanged. The 6b ally turn is unchanged.
- Ammo. Each shot writes one `resource.adjust -1` on the body's ammo pool in the round's writer group. It is an existing op, with no new delta, event, job or save row.
- Melee follows. After round 1, and in any round without a shot, a wielded ranged weapon never strikes. The player strikes with `world.combat.player_attack`, the unarmed profile.
- Any opener. The rule applies to round 1 of every encounter: Attack, a hostile NPC's engage, or a spell's fightBack (mechanics.md 29b, "Kill credit and the fight"). State this as deliberate.
- Budget. A shot spends the player's usual hit draw, plus a damage draw only for variable damage. It adds no draw to the eight-draw round budget (mechanics.md:757; 6b budget note).
- Kill and credit. A shot that kills goes through the existing round path (injure, deathSequence, deathCredit). Nothing new.
- Narration. Optional `world.combat.narration.shot_hit` and `.shot_miss` (TextKeys). Both are required when any item declares `weapon.ranged`; otherwise SCHEMA_VIOLATION, mirroring ally_hit/ally_miss (docs/system/cartridge.md:476-479). Text is content.
- Known limits:
  - Ammo is a counted resource pool, not items. Item consumption needs the foundation consumed-holder change in Beads loka-kgd.83. The 29a ruling that reagents are pools is the precedent.
  - A pool shows in the GameView as a resource meter whose 0 band reads danger (loka-kgd.83 comment), so keep ammo pools to samplers.
  - No adjacent-room shot (owner answer 2). No weapon switching mid-fight.
- Also write: Opt-in (next minor), Book (no new element: two text lines and the existing resource meter; propose sampler wording for the designer), Traps (none applies: the outcome RNG is not variety (trap 5) and the pool is a counted resource, not a status row (trap 11)), Sampler, and the Composition record below.

Add "## Ranged weapon declarations" after "## Damage declarations" (docs/system/cartridge.md:1530). It covers `weapon.ranged.ammo`, a resource ref given as a short key in source and named like allies; the narration pair; and the floor (compiler lib/loka/content/combat.ex, loader kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_combat.ts).

COMPOSITION RECORD (docs/system/architecture.md:89)
- Consumer: the combat round's player and foe opportunities (round.ts ordinaryRound, round_flow.ts packTurns) and round narration.
- Reads: the wielded item's `weapon.ranged`, the ammo pool level, skill usability, statusAllows, and the encounter row's `round`.
- Writes: an ammo `resource.adjust` (existing op). Events, jobs, delta ops and save rows: none new. attack_result is reused, so reactions and the attacker filter see the shot as the player's blow.
- Reused: attack(), attackProfile/equipped, bonused, skills status, statusAllows, resource adjust, injure/deathSequence/deathCredit, the round order, allyOf, narrate, KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID, SCHEMA_VIOLATION.
- New: `WeaponProfile.ranged {ammo}`, the narration keys `shot_hit`/`shot_miss`, one shot predicate shared by both round kinds, the round-1 foe skip, and the next-minor floor. No foundation change.

FILES IN SCOPE (signatures from ast-grep outline; read only these ranges)
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_attack.ts:
  - 49 `export function attack(world, command, mint, encounter_id, row, attacker_id, r, close)`: spend the ammo when shooting.
  - 202 `function equipped(world, body, slot)`.
  - 212 `function attackProfile(world, row, attacker_id, player, r): Profile`: shot uses weapon.attack; otherwise a ranged weapon falls back to player_attack.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round.ts 100 `function ordinaryRound(...)`, order at :113.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_flow.ts:

GOAL
A wielded weapon wears out on each hit and breaks. A forge check sets the forged item's quality band. A smith service mends the weapon for a fee. Sampler acceptance (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:151): "sword breaks after N hits; forge check sets a quality band; the smith repairs it for two pennies and it strikes again".

SPEC GAP: TASK 1 IS THE docs/system AMENDMENT, IN THIS PR, BEFORE CODE
docs/system has no durability, quality or repair mechanic (grep: none). Add the section "## Durability, crafting quality and repair (toolbox row 21)" to docs/system/mechanics.md, after "Movement on a status (toolbox row SR7)". Cite the toolbox row text (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:151: "wear per use, a quality band from the forge check, and a repair service (mechanics/service/) that restores durability for a fee (review 3)"). Also cite docs/reviews/2026-10-10-mechanics-review-3.md:37 (repair merged into row 21) and the archived plan docs/archive/LATER-MECHANICS.md:114 (C3-M03: "two committed uses→0 ... Quality bands/salvage need their own actual selected consumer"). Add "## Durability declarations" to docs/system/cartridge.md after "Harvest tool declarations" (:1635). Use the shape of rows G4/19: Opt-in, Book, Traps, Sampler, Composition record. Settle the design below in the spec text. The PM pre-decided it. Ask only if the code cannot honour it.

PRE-DECIDED DESIGN
1. Durability is a W2 entity fact, not a new pool. WeaponProfile (protocol/entity.schema.json:1083) gets optional `durability: {fact, wear}`. `fact` names this cartridge's bounded int fact with `per_subject: true` and scopes ["instance"]. Safe integer minimum and maximum are required (fact.ts:163 `bounded` needs both). The fact's default is the new weapon's value. `wear` is an int from 1 to 2^31-1. The cartridge owns every number: maximum, default, wear, repair amount and price (owner world-parameters decision, docs/decisions/owner-decision-world-parameters-2026-10-02.md). No engine literal.
2. Wear. In combat@1, when the player's attack hits (`attack_result.hit` true, including a fully resisted `loss: 0`), the wielded weapon's own durable attack struck, and that weapon declares `durability`, the round writes `fact.assign` on that item (subject = the weapon EntityId). The new value is the current value minus `wear`, clamped to the fact minimum (`bounded`). A miss or an unarmed strike does not wear. Hit is the unit ("breaks after N hits").
3. Broken = the fact reads at or below its minimum. Add this clause to the existing usable-weapon test in `attackProfile` (round_attack.ts:212; spec mechanics.md:937-942, "otherwise use the existing unarmed profile"): a broken weapon falls back to `world.combat.player_attack` with no tags (G2 materials, mechanics.md:1873), and it takes no further wear. The Attack offer itself is unchanged. The item stays wielded.
4. Repair. Add a fourth ServiceBenefit, `{kind: "repair", fact, amount}` (protocol/service.schema.json). Its target is the item directly in the actor body's `wield` holder whose `weapon.durability.fact` is `benefit.fact` (the same lookup as round_attack.ts:202 `equipped`; move that helper to a shared place, do not copy it). The new value is the current value plus `amount`, capped at the fact maximum. Refusals, after the existing quote/provider/payment checks and in recovery()'s order:
   - no such wielded item: `invalid_state` with key `service.nothing_to_repair`;
   - value already at the maximum: `invalid_state` with key `service.full_durability`.
   Both refuse before any charge. The cartridge supplies both texts; extend cartridge_services.ts:31 `reasons`. use_service's payload is unchanged: it has no item field, so a weapon carried but not wielded cannot be repaired (state this as a known limit). The GameView offer reuses `availability` (view/services.ts:24) unchanged, so offer and execution share one admission query.
5. Writer ownership. Extend fact.ts:101 `ownership` with the owner 'durability'. A fact named by any item's `weapon.durability.fact` may be assigned only with that owner. A recipe, dialogue or reaction write throws precondition_failed, the same guard as entitlement facts (mechanics.md:1424 "Only service writes its opted entitlement fact"). Combat wear and service repair pass the owner. This prevents the two-writer conflicting_write class seen in batch M2.
6. Quality band: content only, no engine code. The forge is a G4 use recipe (mechanics.md:2273-2285) on the existing blade item, with a check. The outcomes' `fact.assign` sets an enum entity fact `quality` on the target: success gives `fine`, failure gives `crude`. Its consumer is a W6 short variant through `fact_compare {subject: "target"}` (mechanics.md:2056-2069). The recipe policy `fact_compare quality = unforged` stops a re-forge. Known limit, to state in the spec: there are two bands (pass/fail), and quality does not change durability or damage. Add those when content selects that consumer (for example S5's Armorer's test).
7. Floor: these fields need kernel_api at least the next free minor at merge (base installs 1.66 in kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107; sibling M9b rows may claim minors first, so take the next one at merge). A lower floor gives KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at the weapon's `durability` and the service's `benefit`, in both kernels' loaders.

Consumer: combat@1's player attack (round_attack.ts `attack`, `attackProfile`), service@1 `transition`, and the GameView service offer. Reads: wield slot holder custody, the item's WeaponProfile, the entity fact rows and defaults, and the fact bounds. 2. Mechanics untouched. attributes@1 `value` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:29) still adds every worn affect. - Membership. `world.group {member}`: `member` names a bool pair fact (W2: `per_subject: true`, `scopes: ["player"]`). An NPC is in the character's group while that fact is true for (NPC, character); the character is the leader. Join and leave are content: a dialogue's `fact.assign` at the speaker, or a reaction's. Nothing stored is new.
- Co-move. When Move, Flee or a transport moves the body, every living NPC directly in the source room whose member fact is true moves to the same destination in the same writer group, in EntityId order. One place: `travel` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/escort/shared.ts:122; called at movement/sequence.ts:52, transport/shared.ts:89). Find candidates with `npcsIn(world, [source])` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/speech/shared.ts:20) and `value(world, actor, fact, npc)` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:52). A member elsewhere stays put (no fault, no write; it follows again once co-located). The escorted NPC is skipped by the group walk, so it moves once.
- Shared credit and fighting. A member counts as an ally of its leader's character: `ally` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/shared.ts:67) gains the character argument and is true for a listed ally or a member. Attack on a member is refused `invalid_target` and not offered. `allyOf` (:74): the first listed ally living in the encounter room, else the first member there (EntityId order) with an `attack`. One ally turn per round, so the eight-draw budget is unchanged. Party credit follows (credit.ts:123).
- Death writes nothing: membership survives; the body returns alone.
- Known limits: members ride free and pass every exit the leader passes, with no `entity_entered_room` (escort precedent); a schedule or wander still moves a member; NPC-led groups and parties wait for the Realm; members take no combat damage (6b).
- Opt-in 1.71: `world.group` below it is KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at requires.kernel_api.at_least. A `member` that is not a bool per_subject player fact is SCHEMA_VIOLATION at .cartridge.world.group.member, both kernels. - PopulationPlan gains optional `chance`, an integer 1..100 (a percent, as loot `drops.chance`).

- Opportunity: a plan occurrence at a wander boundary (at === wanderDue in runPopulation, crossed

  filter: slot <= target, not living, replacement due reached). Exactly one draw
  `uniform(state.rng, 100, 8)` per opportunity; roll < chance births the first eligible slot only
  (one per opportunity even when cap > 1). No eligible slot = no draw. Non-boundary occurrences
  (replacement due, night boundary off the hour, suppression resume) never birth and never draw.

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)

that merged first, the file's end). docs/system/cartridge.md: extend "## Group declarations"

(grep "lesson_payment"). Decided design:
- world.group gains optional `wage {resource, amount, every}`: resource a DefinitionRef of a
  conserved resource (gain 0, no regen: what `transfer` accepts), amount and every integers >= 1
  (every in LogicalTime seconds). All three required inside wage; additionalProperties false.
- Wage job: a cartridge with world.group.wage gets one fresh-world job {kind 'wage', key
  'group'}, first due at fresh clock + every, minted after the replenish jobs (so cartridges
  without wage keep their ids). Fixed grid like runReplenish: a run at `at` schedules the next
  at at + every; a next time the same advance also crosses returns as `next` (its own drain
  step). Each due settles exactly once; the elapsed host already stops at every pending
  non-calendar job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts:61-70). Wages run whether or not
  anyone is a member (no member = no ops but the reschedule).
- A run pays, in EntityId order, every living NPC whose member fact is true at world.character,
  amount each, from world.body to the NPC, against a running balance: the payable members are
  the longest EntityId-order prefix the player's balance covers (value - k*amount >= minimum)
  and each NPC's row takes (value + amount <= maximum). Ops: one `adjust` per side threaded
  through `levels` (resource.ts:83-105 `adjust(world, entity, resource, by, levels)`): adjust ops
  carry an absolute `to`, so two `transfer` calls from one purse in one proposal would both write
  value - amount. Payment is all-or-nothing per member (no partial wage).
- Unpaid: every living member not paid assigns member false at (world.character, NPC) (fact.ts
  `assigned` with subject, as dialogue/sequence.ts:49). Nothing else: stay/fight keep their
  values (a re-hire restores the old orders, as 22a's dismiss leaves them to content), the NPC
  stays where it is. Dead members are skipped (neither paid nor dismissed).

  player -> dialogue NPC payment, dialogue/payment.ts) without a `skill.acquire` step. Today the
  loader and compiler require exactly one skill.acquire with lesson_payment

- kernel_api: world.group.wage, or a lesson_payment without skill.acquire, needs at least 1.75

waypoints for a fee; the trip ... is instant with no clock change, never a clock skip"). The
06:31 ruling assumed transport routes have no availability gate. They do: every transport names
an ActionDefinition, and every ActionDefinition carries a required `policy`. Transport admission
goes through it: kernel/ts/src/mechanics/transport/shared.ts:33-40 `availability()` ->

a.policy.root, ...)`, else invalid_state), and the GameView offer shows the same refusal
(kernel/ts/src/view/transports.ts:6-45, available false, reason code). So a transport action
whose policy is `visited_count {room: <destination>, at_least: 1}` (policy.ts:83-84, variety@1)
is fast travel between visited waypoints. No engine change. Deliver a sampler, a test and the spec.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-fast-travel off toolbox/batch-m10 at the head the PM gives (b6156e83 = 04f46aaf
plus W9 sleep 1.76). Own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push;

notes:
[Pi · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · session 01a12efa]
Written 2026-10-12 12:05 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

BRIEF loka-kgd.121: Toolbox row 41, decay (batch M10, wave 4). Size M, one run, no split.
kernel_api 1.78 (PM assignment, plan 06:31 "1.78 only if engine": it is engine, below). Row 41
moved M13 -> M10 (PM 2026-10-11 19:09: content only on G3 + W1, both done, so decay lands with
19b restock); the toolbox table edit is the PM's, in the batch PR.

GOAL
Toolbox row 41 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:180: "a status with expiry on a thing (G3) whose expiry
reaction (W1) moves it to the terminal consumed holder"; sampler "fish spoils after a day while
smoked fish lasts; a corpse and a dropped rag are cleaned up"). The plan asked the brief to
confirm a reaction step can move a thing to 19b's reserve; none can. The reaction apply steps
(protocol/reaction.schema.json apply oneOf) are fact.assign/adjust, quest.*, population.suppress,
status.apply/cure, barrier.set, experience.grant: nothing moves an item. And D4's consumed holder
takes only edible items from a body (kernel/ts/src/foundation/compose.ts:243-262 and the
containment invariant). So row 41 adds one reaction step, `item.move`, which moves the event's
subject item to an authored room; a sealed room is then both the decay sink and a 19b replenish
reserve, closing 19b's known limit ("a finite reserve is the lifetime supply until decay (row
41) feeds it back", mechanics.md Replenish). Every number (durations, room, grid) from the cartridge.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-decay off toolbox/batch-m10 at the head the PM gives (b6156e83 = 04f46aaf plus
W9 sleep 1.76). Own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted
CI on the head (developer.md step 1). Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts;
prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it; `elixir bin/contracts.exs --check`; `node
bin/check_ts_size.mjs` from the repo root AFTER committing (tracked files only); `elixir
bin/check_size.exs`; mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix credo
--strict. Never end a turn waiting on a bg_run. No new import cycle (below).

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
docs/system/mechanics.md: append "## Decay (toolbox row 41)" after "## Sleep (toolbox row W9)"
(the file end, :2595-2608 on b6156e83); add `item.move` to the reaction@1 step list (section
:581; the subject table text near :616); rewrite the Replenish known limit (:2510-2526) to point
at row 41. docs/system/cartridge.md: an "item.move" declaration paragraph after the W22
barrier.set reaction-step paragraph (:1695). Decided design:
- New apply step `{op: "item.move", room: DefinitionRef}` (both required, additionalProperties
  false), after experience.grant in protocol/reaction.schema.json (:625-634).
- Behaviour: the step reads the rule's subject (reaction.ts SUBJECT map :179-190; status_expired,
  status_applied and status_ticked give the status holder; item_acquired the acquirer; entity_died
  the victim; item_dropped none, so the actor's body). If the subject is an item entity whose
  container is not already that room, the step emits one entity.transfer of it from its current
  container (room, body, NPC or container item) to the room, in the delivery's writer group. Any
  other subject (body, NPC, room) or an item already there: nothing. No event, no narration, no
  capacity or reach check (the room is an authored sink). If an eaten (consumed) item can still be
  a status holder at expiry (probe it; see FILES), the step also does nothing for an item in
  world.consumed; if the eat removes the status row, no guard and say so.

  the manifest at_least) in both kernels; the room must resolve (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at the
  step's `room`). world.ts kernel_api becomes '1.78'.

  narration.expired is said only when the holder is the player's body (status/job.ts runStatus
  :31-75), so a spoiled fish says nothing.

  re-applies its status, which refreshes the end (status/shared.ts:113-165), so decay restarts
  on every pickup; a status that expires while a `when` refuses the move leaves the item where it
  is with no status (nothing re-arms it); corpse decay is not in this row (created corpses carry
  keywords, not tags, so status.apply `tag` cannot reach them, and entity_died's subject is the
  victim; follow-up issue); moving an equipped item is whatever entity.transfer does today (see

chapters, corpse decay follow-up. Reads: the reaction subject, the item's container. Writes:

title: Toolbox row G7: access locks (enter, traverse, get, put) — batch M11
description: docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row G7. Brief in notes.
notes:
[Claude Code · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · session 01FtwqZjvGA5A9sL3d8WjiJz]
Written 2026-10-13 UTC in Claude Code by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (drafted, adopted by the PM)

BRIEF loka-kgd.123: Toolbox row G7, access locks (batch M11, wave 1). Size M, one run, no
split. kernel_api 1.78 (engine: new schema fields and three admission hooks). Line numbers below are
on toolbox/batch-m10 b6156e83; M10 wave 4 (rows 32, 41) lands before toolbox/batch-m11 is cut, so
docs line numbers shift. Re-find a range by its heading or function name, never by number alone.

GOAL
Toolbox row G7 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:161; sampler "a guest may enter an owned hut but not take
from its chest; revoke the grant and entry refuses; a stranger is refused"). Today an action's
policy gates a whole verb (commands/actions.ts refusal :220-259), and a barrier's `opens_when` gates
one door's open (barrier/rule.ts:93). Nothing gates one exit, room or container per actor. G7 adds
an optional `locks` map: an access type to a VersionedPolicy, on an exit, a room or an item. The
existing evaluator reads it (mechanics/policy.ts `holds`) at the shared admission of the matching
verb. Grants and roles are W2 pair facts (mechanics.md:2170 "A G7 grant is a pair fact on the thing
and the grantee"), written by the writers that already exist. The design adds no policy leaf and no
grant command (see Decided design and PM questions 1-2). Every world value (who is granted, which
role opens what) comes from the cartridge.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m11-locks off toolbox/batch-m11 at the head the PM gives. Own worktree under
worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted CI on the head (developer.md step 1).
Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts; prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it;
`elixir bin/contracts.exs --check`; `node bin/check_ts_size.mjs` from the repo root AFTER committing
(it reads tracked files only); `elixir bin/check_size.exs`; mix format --check-formatted, mix compile
--warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict. Never end a turn waiting on a bg_run. No new import cycle
(locks.ts imports policy.ts; check that nothing policy.ts reaches imports locks.ts back).

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
docs/system/mechanics.md: append "## Access locks (toolbox row G7)" at the file end (after Decay,
row 41). In "## barrier@1" (:63-83) add one sentence: an `opens_when` is the barrier's open lock, and
G7 adds no second spelling of it. In "## containment@1" (:85-151) add one sentence each: take
honours `get` locks, put honours `put` locks. docs/system/cartridge.md: append "## Access lock
declarations" at the file end. Cite architecture.md:89-128 ("Building mechanics by composition")
in the composition record. Decided design:
- Fields (schema, both kernels): `Connection.locks {traverse}` (protocol/room.schema.json Connection
  :17), `RoomDefinition.locks {enter}` (:391), `ItemDefinition.locks {get?, put?}`
  (protocol/entity.schema.json :152). Each is an object of VersionedPolicy, minProperties 1,
  additionalProperties false, so an unknown or misplaced access type is a SCHEMA_VIOLATION. A `put`
  lock needs `container: true` on the item; the loader refuses it otherwise (SCHEMA_VIOLATION
  invalid_value at `.locks.put`, both kernels).

description: Batch M1 of the mechanics track (epic loka-kgd): one draft branch toolbox/batch-m1, worktree lokacore-wt-m1, one commit (or small set) per item, in order: foundation item 4, row 1, row 2. 2026-10-09 s9 handoff: not started (developer context limit). Questions for PM before code: (1) formula shape: cartridge-owned linear per-point table per derived stat (hit chance, damage min/max, hp max, carry grams) with baseline? (2) dummies = NPCs (NPCs have no attributes today) or two player ancestries? (3) hp max live from attribute or fixed at creation? (4) rounding rule; (5) opt-in only (Chapter 1 frozen). Reuse: attributes/shared.ts value(), combat/round_attack.ts attackProfile, containment/shared.ts carrying max_grams.
PM decisions 2026-10-09 (mechanics-lane autonomy, owner): (1) cartridge-owned linear table per derived stat: base + sum(per_point[attr] * (value - pivot)), integer coefficients, optional divisor; no engine numbers. (2) dummies = two sampler ancestries (STR 5 vs 15); attackProfile and carrying are player-side, attributes value() unchanged, no NPC attributes. (3) HP max SPLIT OUT: it changes resource@1 bounds (contract), own follow-up item with a decision record + second opinion; kgd.3 = hit, damage, carry. (4) rounding = floor toward minus infinity (Math.floor / Integer.floor_div), one negative fixture case on both kernels; hit chance clamped 0..100, damage and carry clamped >= 0. (5) opt-in only; Chapter 1 hashes unchanged.
2026-10-09 dev: built on toolbox/batch-m1 (7f62656c..0bc4e18e). Readings: base = authored number (profile chance/damage, carry.max_grams); pivot per term; divisor divides the sum only. Deviation from (4): negative floor case is a TS literal row (nimble -5/2 -> -3), no protocol fixture or Elixir evaluator (Elixir has no consumer, ADR-074); Elixir parity = compiler checks. PM to confirm.

description: Owner 2026-10-09 (verbatim): 'can you get fable to audit the proposed 2 lane workflow with github free CI, to optimize for speed of development since we are in preproduction, and less damage on my personal m1 processor'. title: Toolbox row 19b: replenish primitive (harvest regrowth, shop restock, any finite holder) — batch M10
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-11: regrowth plus a general restocking mechanic.

PM design (decided, mechanics lane): no item minting. One composable job kind 'replenish': {from: a roomless reserve holder, to: a holder (harvest seam, shop shelf, chest, room), item template, cap, every: interval, when: optional leaf}. Each due tick moves up to N item instances reserve -> target until the target holds cap. Items stay conserved, so saves, receipts and conservation invariants need no new item kind.
Covers: harvest regrowth (row 19), shop restock (B3/B5 finite stock), refilling chests/forage, later W11 stock-sensitive prices and NPC trade jobs.
Loop with decay (row 41): a decay expiry may move a thing to the reserve instead of the terminal consumed holder, so spoiled stock feeds regrowth (ponytail: a finite reserve is total lifetime supply unless decay feeds it back).
Open for the brief: per-tick count; does a refill of a shelf show to the player (Book line)?; Book wording must not promise regrowth times (book-ui.md:549).
Also fix MECHANICS-TOOLBOX row 19 text, which cites loka-kgd.84 instead of this issue.
notes:
[Pi · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · M10 planner]
Written 2026-10-12 06:28 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

BRIEF: toolbox row 19b, replenish primitive (batch M10, wave 1). Size M, one run, no split. kernel_api 1.72 (loka-btpd).

GOAL
Owner ask 2026-10-11 (this issue): regrowth plus restocking. The PM design above stands: no minting; conserved items move from a reserve to a target up to a cap. Covers row 19's "Regrowth. Not built" (docs/system/mechanics.md:2295), shop restock, any finite holder. Row 41 and loka-kgd.107.3 build on it.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-replenish off toolbox/batch-m10 (PM gives the head); own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted CI on the head. Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts; prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it.

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
Add "## Replenish (toolbox row 19b)" at the end of docs/system/mechanics.md (6b bullet shape) and "## Replenish declarations" in docs/system/cartridge.md after "Harvest tool declarations". Replace the Regrowth bullet (:2295) with a link here. Decided design (answers this issue's open questions):
- Declaration. A top-level section `replenish`, keyed like `populations`. Each entry is `{items, from, to, cap, count, every}`:
  - `items`: an identity set of authored item refs, as `harvest.items`.
  - `from` and `to`: an `ItemLocation` (protocol/entity.schema.json:6; room, npc or item; `template` refused).
  - `cap`, `count`, `every`: integers of at least 1; `every` in clock units. Numbers are content.
- Job. One pending job per entry, `job {kind: "replenish", key}`, first due at start + every. The seed is appended after firstClock in `firstJobs` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/behavior.ts:59), so existing cartridges mint the same ids. Dispatch is one line in `decideAt` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts:42).
- Run. held = `selected(world, items, to, Infinity, steps)` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/stock.ts:5). Then move `min(count, cap - held)` instances from `selected(world, items, from, …)`, in its EntityId order, by `entity.transfer`. Then `job.complete`, and the next job at due_time + every, a fixed grid. A next due time the advance also crosses runs as its own drain step, as `scheduledJob`'s `crossed`/`next` (schedule/rule.ts:119-133). An empty reserve or a full target moves nothing and still reschedules.
- Host. The elapsed host stops at every non-calendar job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts:67): each interval runs once however an absence is chunked. No host change.
- Silent: no line, no event; the Book never promises a time (book-ui.md:549).
- Known limits: a finite reserve is the lifetime supply until row 41 feeds it back; no `when` gate yet; the reserve is any authored holder (a sealed room; reach.ts lists it unreachable).
- Opt-in 1.72 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at requires.kernel_api.at_least). Both kernels: a template location or `from` equal to `to` is SCHEMA_VIOLATION; an unresolved ref UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.
- Also: Book (no new element), Traps (trap 1 holds: due times on the clock), Sampler, composition record.

COMPOSITION RECORD
Consumer: schedule@1 run_job; Harvest, shops and the GameView read the result unchanged. Reads: containers. Writes: `entity.transfer`, `job.complete`, `job.schedule` (existing). Events and save rows: none new. Reused: `selected`, firstJobs, the crossed-hour drain, ItemLocation. New: the `replenish` section, its job kind, `runReplenish`, the 1.72 floor. No foundation change.

FILES (outline signatures; read only these ranges)
- New kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/replenish.ts: `firstReplenish`, `runReplenish`.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/behavior.ts:59 firstJobs; kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts:42 decideAt, :98 scheduledJob (model).
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/stock.ts:5 selected.
- Loader: new kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_replenish.ts, registered beside the other checks. Compiler: lib/loka/content/source.ex:123 (section map), new lib/loka/content/replenish.ex (short-key expansion, same checks).
- protocol/cartridge.schema.json:310 (beside `populations`); protocol/fixtures/invalid.json; regenerate kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts.
- kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107 kernel_api '1.72'.
- New cartridges/replenish_sampler, kernel/ts/test/replenish.test.ts, test/loka/content_replenish_test.exs.
- docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md: add row 19b after row 19 (M10, done #N); row 19's "loka-kgd.84" becomes loka-kgd.85. Regenerate docs/toolbox.gen.json, docs/system-graph.gen.json.

SAMPLER
- Mine: a harvest detail `seam` with items ore_01..ore_05, no tool. The mine holds ore_01 and ore_02.
- Store (no exits) holds ore_03..05 and a stone.
- `seam_regrowth`: {items ore_01..05, from store, to mine, cap 2, count 1, every 3600}.
- Trader: an NPC holding nothing. A crate in the store holds apple_01.
- `shelf`: {items [apple_01], from crate (item), to trader (npc), cap 1, count 1, every 3600}.

ACCEPTANCE (replenish.test.ts; literal ore counts)
A. Harvest twice at 0, then Harvest is refused not_found. Wait to 3600: mine 1, store 2. Wait to 7200: mine 2, store 1. Wait to 10800: mine 2, store 1. The stone stays in the store throughout.
B. The two harvests, then one wait 0 to 10800: mine 2, store 1 (the same as A, step by step).
C. No harvest, wait to 3600: mine 2, store 3.
D. Wait to 3600: the trader holds apple_01 and the crate is empty.
E. Both kernels: the floor, a template location, from equal to to, an unresolved item. Schema fixtures: cap 0, an unknown field; then the schema mutant sweep (docs/lessons/contracts.md).
F. A cartridge without `replenish` gets no new job; existing pins and Chapter 1 receipts are unchanged.

RED CONTROLS: ignore cap (C store 2); ignore count (A mine 2 at 3600); no item filter (the stone moves); no reschedule (A mine 1 at 7200); no drain step (B mine 1).

FOCUSED RUNS: node --test replenish, harvest_tool and schedule tests; mix test the new Elixir test (--force for mutants).

READ: AGENTS.md (Simplicity, Writing tests), developer.md, docs/lessons/mechanics.md, storage.md, contracts.md.

OUT: row 41, a `when` gate, the ledger listing replenish (.107.3), mobile/authority, Elixir runtime.

SCOPE TRIGGER (ask the PM): any item minting; a new save section, op or event; a mobile/authority or save-recovery change; fresh-world id changes for existing cartridges; two docs/system clauses disagreeing.

HANDOFF near 180k tokens.

PARALLEL: wave 1 with G8 and loka-kgd.107.2 (additive overlaps only). Row 9 edits decideAt/firstJobs too: it runs after this merges.

comments.author: raymondluong
comments.text: Fable consultation summary: subtle = delayed, indirect, discovered not announced, no visible score. Patterns: world keeps the score via variants/prices/schedules; kindness pays off elsewhere later (Wat's cloak); cruelty echoes via rumour hops + codex deduction (letter burn); fuse statuses for days-later consequences (strongbox); body habits (draught tremor vs practice); sound cues as consequence; scars as memory. Avoid meters, instant feedback, symmetry, narrator adjectives, progress gates. Gaps (small): delayed reaction idiom or 'after' field, hidden statuses, loka-kgd.22 NPC move, kgd.79 attacker filter, time-since leaf, reaction log line (verify). First experiment: one content slice in the social district (patterns 3+4), two saves deliver vs burn, ask 'did I find out or was I told?'

title: Marketing: paid-UGC creator pilot after soft launch (Wispr Flow playbook, scoped)
description:
Tabled marketing strategy (owner 2026-10-10; Fable advice). Source: Wispr Flow paid-UGC creator-ads thread (creators paid % of ad spend plus a guaranteed minimum; one creator per segment gap; no look-alike ads because Meta Andromeda clusters similar creatives; small coached group run like a sales team).

Transfers: creative diversity is the lever we control; one creator per gap; small coached group; keyword-search recruiting (BookTok, IF, MUD, cosy games).
Does not transfer yet: no spend, no pricing, a one-chapter game cannot supply 500+ ads a month, and a % of spend model needs real spend first.

Prereqs: open-test build, store listing, "finished Chapter 1" analytics, a Chapter 2 price or waitlist, landing page.
Pilot (6 weeks, $3-6k incl. $1.5-3k Meta spend): 4-6 creators, flat $150-300/video plus a small per-install bonus, 2-3 videos each. Gaps: BookTok reader ("a novel you play"), ex-MUD nostalgia, cosy no-timer gamer, commute/offline reader, optionally one non-US English market. No two videos with the same hook or shot.
Measure: CPI, click-to-install, D1/D7, Chapter 1 completion, Chapter 2 intent per creator. Kill: CPI > ~$3 with D7 < 15% after $2k, or no gap beats the others by 2x. Thresholds are general rules of thumb, not Loka data.
Open: monetization model; content runway (showcase / Chapter 2); is the IF/MUD creator pool deep enough, or should author-led organic (dev log, BookTok) find the hook first?
Not before M8 and the showcase; owner decides timing.

title: Monetization: free chapter 1 + one-time unlock, paid cartridges, ethics guardrails (Right Livelihood)
description:
Tabled monetization model (owner 2026-10-10; Fable advice). Owner constraint (paraphrased): no predatory design, no pay-to-win, no gambling-like mechanics; follow Buddhist Right Livelihood (honest trade, no harm or deception, no exploiting compulsion, fair value).

Recommended launch: chapter 1 free and complete; one-time unlock for the next chapter(s) at $4.99-7.99; later cartridges $2.99-4.99 each plus a complete-book bundle. Patron tier with cosmetic-only book themes and a colophon credit comes in a later release. Creator marketplace later still (needs builder guide, store policy, revenue share, moderation).
Considered: premium upfront (cleanest, but discovery-limited).

Ethics guardrails (adopt as a product rule when the owner decides):
1. Price visible before any tap that starts a purchase.
2. Nothing purchasable is random, timed, scarce or expiring.
3. No purchase changes difficulty, stats, odds, resources or hints; paid content differs only in story.
4. Free content is complete; no mid-scene paywall; one offer shown per chapter end, no reminders.
5. No energy, streaks, daily-login rewards or pull-back notifications.
6. Refund link in app; honor platform refunds without friction.
7. No in-game ads; no tracking beyond what store receipts need.
8. Marketing claims are checked against the shipped build.

Depends on: PREP-03 store-policy review (before any price is published) and an IAP slice in mobile. Pairs with loka-marketing-ugc-pilot-5mrn: creators sell the free chapter; pay per video plus a share of unlock revenue, never per install; real current-build footage only, no urgency language, price stated if buying is mentioned, sponsorship disclosed.
Conversion figures are industry rules of thumb, not Loka data. Owner decides timing.

title: Kernel wait across two listed hours of one NPC faults nonfuture_job
description: A single wait command whose advance crosses two consecutive daily_schedule hours of one NPC faults nonfuture_job: the first run_job schedules its successor at the next listed hour (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts, nextHour from the job's due time), which is not after the advance's horizon (foundation/compose_job.ts). Repro on toolbox/batch-m6 89a277c8: cartridges/schedule_sampler, wait from 07:00 until 13:00 (hours 8 and 12); cartridges/rumour_sampler, wait from 16:30 until 18:30. The host's elapsed settlement ends a step at each due job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts boundary), but a player wait goes to step whole. Found in loka-kgd.57; tests there wait one hour at a time.

comments.author: raymondluong
comments.text: Fix pushed on toolbox/m6-waitfix, head 29d9746e (base 89a277c8). Scope: the fault is older than W10. kernel/ts/test/schedule.test.ts on main has pinned it since 801aa00d (Bram, 19:00 then 06:00). Chapter 1 (ashmere_missing_child, real_elapsed) cannot hit it: player Wait and recipe skips are off there, and elapsed.ts boundary() ends each step at the earliest non-clock job. Chapter 1 does have NPCs with two listed hours inside one long advance (gareth 18/22, ash 12/20). Root cause: scheduledJob put the successor at nextHour(row.due_time), and the composer refuses a due time at or before the advance target. Fix in kernel schedule/rule.ts: a run takes hour = max(due, calendar lastHour(clock)). The NPC goes to that hour's room and the successor is nextHour(hour). The arrival event keeps the job's time, so one run has one cause time. Intermediate hours collapse. The schedule.test.ts fault test is replaced by a test over 2 and 3 hours. In the sim pin, wait to MAX_SAFE now faults evaluator_error (successor past 2^53) where it used to fault nonfuture_job. mechanics.md schedule paragraph updated. Public repo: standard runners free; mind the 20-concurrent-job limit.

title: Research: local AI in the mobile app (familiar companion, NPC dialogue, subtle LLM uses)

Questions: (1) which ideas fit the kernel's rules: deterministic replay, owner-save bytes, receipts as the record of truth, one difficulty, fixed time; where an LLM can only phrase or retrieve, never decide or write durable state; (2) the familiar as a view over receipts and knowledge rows (retrieval, no new save data) vs a stored memory; spoiler and hallucination guards (answers cite events the player saw); (3) NPC dialogue: free text over authored dialogue graphs (intent mapping to existing choices) vs generated lines bounded by cartridge facts; (4) on-device model options for iOS and Android in an Expo/React Native app (size, latency, battery, licence), and a no-model fallback so the game is complete without it; (5) other subtle uses (narration variety on W7, hint phrasing on W23, accessibility, recap on reopen); (6) risks and a smallest first experiment. title: Storybook long-haul tweaking: live polish sessions + own picker
description:

Also: make our own Tidewave-like element picker and delete Tidewave; screenshot baselines later.
Goal: Storybook as a long-haul UI tweaking environment. Batches: W1 process + scripts, H1 hardening (parallel with W1), P1 picker with live tweak loop (after W1), then live polish sessions. Max two agents at once (load).
Live polish session lane: session branch + worktree served to the owner's Storybook (HMR); each owner prompt from the picker is applied at once by a resumed Fable designer (style code, tokens, catalogue line); owner's look = design review; 'Close batch' -> one Opus reviewer quick pass + one pre-push hook -> PM merges; owner Storybook back to main. Mechanics/save/protocol/engine items leave the session as normal Beads issues. Batches stay open liberally; close only for critical items or too much complexity (PM may suggest closing in the picker panel).
notes:
Owner 2026-10-09 (paraphrased): use a lower model for small nits, Fable for overall design; PM decides. PM ruling: PM classifies each picker prompt. NIT (Sonnet designer): one place, existing tokens only: swap which token a style uses, alignment, a value inside one component, wording of a label. DESIGN (Fable designer): anything that changes a token value (global), adds a token or component, touches hierarchy/typography/colour/composition, spans several components, or is a feel request ('make it calmer'). Sonnet escalates to Fable when a nit needs a token or rule change. Owner can force with a 'fable:' or 'quick:' prefix. Panel shows which model did each item. At Close batch, if the batch holds 5+ Sonnet nits, Fable skims the nit diffs for consistency (one short pass) before the Opus review. Out of scope (mechanics/save/engine) -> Beads.

title: Book: combat closure hides the kill, death and inn-return lines
description: Showcase combat playtest (loka-y6yg.7) G1/G2/U1. When an encounter closes, its closing lines are never shown: the kill ("Your foe falls."), the player's death ("You fall.") and the inn return. Repro (real Book over toolbox_showcase, pulsed every 3 s): Drill Yard north, Attack the boar unarmed. Rounds 1-4 show on the Combat page; at round 5 the page goes straight to Crossroads Inn at hp 10 with no line anywhere. Cause: combat narration is routed only to the combat log (book/presenter.ts:85, book/received.ts:60-75), Combat.tsx:52 returns null once view.combat is gone and model.ts:72-73 drops the combat page in the same update; book-ui.md:430-438 says combat narration never enters the World log, closure and death included. So the fatal round's text has nowhere to show. Smallest fix (spec change, designer first): when the encounter closes, keep the Combat page with its log and one Continue card until the player taps it (dialogue pattern); or copy the closing receipt's combat lines into the World log. Either way the playtester's "fights are a black box" goes away with no engine change. Note: per-round Attack/Wait cards are not missing; rounds are timed (interval 150 at rate 50, about 3 s real time; mechanics.md:730-743, book-ui.md:419-424).

title: Web preview: time did not advance during the combat playtest; each press caught up whole fights and ticks
description: Showcase combat playtest (loka-y6yg.7) G1/G3/G4/G7. In the web preview playtest, rounds and bleed ticks did not advance while the player read: screenshot 24 shows the Combat page at hp 10 with no rounds after think time, then one press (Look, Flee, Take, Eat) ran every overdue round or tick first and the press landed on a changed world. Reproduced exactly in the real Book by advancing the clock 15 s without pulses: Look jumps to the inn (death) with no line; Flee prints "You can't do that: not now." on the World page (G4); with a poultice held and bleeding, 40 s without pulses then Eat: hp 8 to 7, bleeding expired in the catch-up, Eat refuses "not now" and its card vanishes (G7, the playtester's 6 to 4). With 3-second pulses all of these behave (rounds log one by one; Flee and Eat succeed). The engine is right (due work before input, mechanics.md:212). Open question: why the web clock did not pulse. Candidates: (1) App.tsx:176 useElapsed pauses on AppState background, which on web follows document.visibilityState, so an occluded or unfocused Chrome window in the computer-use harness stops time; (2) the showcase is the first cartridge with recap_after, so the clock waits for booked (App.tsx:173, shell.subscribed in book/updates.ts:34); no stall found by reading, needs a live check. Fix: verify in a focused web tab (Combat page should log a round every 3 s); if (1), record it as a playtest harness rule (keep the tab visible); if (2), fix the booking order. Also consider: a refusal after a press-time catch-up should say what changed (designer, U3).
